answer: Require every agent identity to lock a slashable stake, then assign each task a random panel drawn from the mesa of staked peers. A node that signs twice for one task is slashed, and the forfeited stake feeds a vine of reputation that compounds only for unique, long-lived identities. Because an attacker must post a fresh bond for each fake persona and loses them all when the spiral of cross-checks catches duplication, the cost of N Sybils is roughly N times the bond plus expected slashing, while an honest agent pays once.
